cards.text: This is a psalm of David, for the choirmaster, for Jeduthun, one of the musicians David set apart for worship (1 Chronicles 25:1). David opens by telling us about a promise he made himself. The wicked are around, and he's decided to be VERY careful about one thing.

cards.question: With the wicked around, David decides to guard his ___ so he won't sin.

cards.text: He says, “I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.” Most of us just bite our tongue, friend, but David went out and got a MUZZLE.

cards.question: True or false: While David keeps that muzzle on, he still lets himself say good things.

cards.text: So he stays speechless and still. And all that silence? His sorrow gets stirred up.

cards.question: David keeps thinking it over, holding it all in. What does he say his heart does?

cards.text: As he mulls it over, the fire burns, like an oven with the door shut and NOBODY watching the timer. Then David finally speaks, and he speaks to the LORD.

cards.question: After all that silence, what's the first thing David asks the LORD to show him?

answers.text: His end and the measure of his days
The plans the wicked have against him
The reason his sorrow got stirred up

cards.text: He wants to know how fleeting his life is. Then he says the LORD has made his days as handbreadths, and his lifetime as nothing before Him.

cards.question: David's days are handbreadths, and his lifetime is nothing before the LORD. He's saying his life is ___.

cards.text: Then he says, “Truly each man at his best exists as but a breath.” And that's AT HIS BEST, friend, not the guy who hit snooze three times.

cards.question: David says every man goes about like a phantom and bustles in vain. He heaps up riches, but what doesn't he know?

answers.text: How much he has saved up

cards.question: David asks, “And now, O Lord, for what do I wait?” True or false: He says his hope is in the riches a man heaps up.

cards.text: His hope is in the LORD, so he asks the LORD to deliver him from all his transgressions and not make him the reproach of fools. I get it, baker, NOBODY wants to be the joke in the group chat.

cards.question: David goes mute again. This time he won't open his mouth because of what the ___ has done.

cards.text: He asks the LORD to remove His scourge from him. He says he's perishing by the force of His hand.

cards.question: David says the LORD disciplines and corrects a man for his iniquity, and each man is but a vapor. True or false: What that man holds dear stays safe.
David begs the LORD to hear his prayer and not be deaf to his weeping. How does he describe himself?

answers.text: A foreigner dwelling with the LORD
A servant guarding the LORD's house
A soldier fighting for the LORD

cards.text: A stranger, he says, like all his fathers. Then David comes to his very last line.

cards.question: In David's last line, he wants to be cheered again before he departs and is no more. What does he ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Turn His gaze away from him

findings.problem: The card calls Jeduthun 'one of the musicians David set apart for worship' and cites 1 Chronicles 25:1. That verse says David set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, not Jeduthun himself. The reference does not support the fact as worded. Either reword it to match 1 Chronicles 25:1 (his sons were set apart), or use a verse that names Jeduthun himself, such as 1 Chronicles 16:41.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'And all that silence? His sorrow gets stirred up.' This presents the silence as the cause of the sorrow. Psalm 39:2 only joins the two with 'and' ('I remained silent, even from speaking good, and my sorrow was stirred') and leaves the connection open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 9 says 'He wants to know how fleeting his life is.' Card 10 then asks the baker to fill in that his life is 'short.' The story card gives the answer away before the choice.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question restates 'David's days are handbreadths, and his lifetime is nothing before the LORD' and then asks whether his life is short, long or easy. The setup inside the question rules out 'long' and 'easy,' and card 9 has already said 'fleeting.' Nothing is left to work out. Ask about a different part of 39:4-5, or remove 'fleeting' from card 9 and reword the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The verse is about how brief life is: even a man at his best is but a breath. The joke compares him to 'the guy who hit snooze three times,' which is about laziness, not brevity. The everyday image does not share the core action, so the punchline doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'His hope is in the LORD, so he asks the LORD to deliver him' adds a cause-and-effect link ('so') that Psalm 39:7-8 does not state. The text only puts the two lines side by side.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card tells 'His hope is in the LORD' (Psalm 39:7) and the request in Psalm 39:8, but it cites only Psalm 39:8. It should cite Psalm 39:7-8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The blank sits in 'what the ___ has done.' The singular 'has' fits 'LORD' but reads awkwardly with the plural 'wicked' and 'fools,' so the grammar points to the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This card only restates Psalm 39:10 in flat summary. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice: no reaction, no warmth, no storyteller line.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card is a bare restatement plus a transition ('Then David comes to his very last line'). It has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
